kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore adventures in Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Our adventure selection for Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay includes an extensive itinerary through eight South American countries. The Argentine section involves walks at Iguazu Falls, Ecuador brings Quito and a boat excursion in the Galapagos, while Uruguay is represented by a day trip to Montevideo. The programme's most demanding high-altitude 4x4 stages actually take place in Bolivia. Find out where physical preparation is really needed and how walking excursions, island journeys and an overland vehicle expedition differ.
---

## What adventures really await in these three countries

**The Argentina–Ecuador–Uruguay combination represents three main countries within an extended journey, not a standalone sporting tour of those three countries.** Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day itinerary through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Besides the three named destinations, it covers Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia.

Adventure is a secondary interest of this programme; its primary themes are culture and nature. This matters when choosing a trip: visiting [Iguazu in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) requires active movement, but this tour does not include a dedicated multi-day trek in Argentina, white-water rafting in Uruguay or an ascent of an Ecuadorian volcano.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

| Country | What happens |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Walks at Iguazu, then the capital |
| Uruguay | Ferry and Montevideo sightseeing |
| Ecuador | High-altitude Quito, Galapagos and a boat trip |

All options across this geography without the theme filter appear in the [Argentina + Ecuador + Uruguay selection](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador_uruguay/). If physical activity is the priority, also explore our [multi-country adventure tours](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Argentine Iguazu: walking near the waterfalls

The published itinerary first visits the Brazilian side of Iguazu and then the **Argentine side with a Russian-speaking guide in a group**, followed by a flight to Buenos Aires. These are different national parks on opposite sides of the border. On the Argentine side, walkways and viewing platforms offer close-up views of the falls and subtropical forest.

Iguazu is a UNESCO World Heritage site, recognised in part for its waterfalls and surrounding forest ecosystems. Yet **walking along the park's established trails is not the same as a technical trek**. It is more important to consider time spent on your feet, heat and humidity, slippery sections, exposure to spray and your ability to keep up with the group's route.

Afterwards, the journey moves to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for a city tour and tango show. This day is best seen as a cultural break between intensive nature stages, without adding sporting activities that are not advertised in the programme.

## Uruguay: crossing the estuary and exploring a city, not a sporting stage

In Uruguay, the itinerary includes **a day trip from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/)**: an early transfer to the port, a ferry journey, sightseeing with an English-speaking guide, free time and the return trip. It offers a welcome change of country and urban environment, but does not advertise trekking, canyoning, surfing or other standalone adventure activities in Uruguay.

The demands here are logistical: an early start, port formalities, boarding the ferry, the excursion and the return journey, all within one day. Travellers seeking active days in Uruguay's natural surroundings would need an additional itinerary and a longer stay. It would be inaccurate to present a brief city visit as a ready-made adventure.

## Ecuador: from Quito's altitude to ocean islands

The Ecuadorian stage begins with a Lima–Quito flight. [Quito and the Cotopaxi area](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) lie in the Andes; the capital's historic centre is approximately 2,850 metres above sea level. The itinerary includes a city and equator-line excursion, **but no ascent of Cotopaxi is advertised**. Altitude can affect how travellers feel even on an ordinary walk, especially after a long flight.

Next comes the flight to the Galapagos and accommodation on [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The marine excursion follows **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrion. One option is confirmed, rather than all the listed islands being visited. After the island section, travellers return to the mainland via Guayaquil.

Activity levels in the Galapagos depend on the landing site and walking trail, time aboard the boat, sea conditions and the rules of the protected area. Comfortable shoes and sun protection are essential; anyone prone to seasickness should discuss the boat journey in advance. Above all, this is **an introduction to the archipelago's protected natural environment**. The catalogue of [Ecuador wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) is useful when comparing programmes where observing animals is the main goal.

## Where the real high-altitude adventures take place on the longer tour

The most active overland section of the 32-day itinerary lies **between Uruguay and Ecuador, in other countries along the route**. After Santiago de Chile, travellers head to San Pedro de Atacama, cross into Bolivia and visit high-altitude lagoons, desert landscapes and the Uyuni area in 4×4 vehicles. Later stages include La Paz, Tiwanaku, Lake Titicaca and Peru.

This is the essential difference from a short Argentina–Uruguay–Ecuador trip. Omitting Chile, Bolivia and Peru would remove most of the high-altitude 4x4 expedition and require a new sequence of flights. Keeping the entire itinerary means packing and preparing for very different conditions: humid Iguazu, cool highlands and marine crossings in the Galapagos.

## Preparing for this combination

**Start by deciding what matters most:** walks beside waterfalls and Galapagos wildlife, or an extended vehicle expedition through the Andes. That decision determines whether you need the full 32-day journey and how many days should remain outside the three named countries.

For the actual programme, physical effort, long transfers and rest intervals should be discussed in advance. Montevideo requires time for the ferry and border formalities, Quito calls for altitude awareness, and the Galapagos depend on marine logistics and the confirmed island excursion option. Entry and transit requirements must be checked for the traveller's nationality and the full sequence of countries; a themed travel selection cannot replace that verification.

Ada Tours helps determine the order of stops, coordinate connections, excursion days and a slower pace where necessary. If you wish to visit only these three countries, a custom programme can be discussed; the conditions and price of the eight-country tour do not automatically apply to it.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay

### Does this combination include multi-day trekking?

The published itinerary contains no independent multi-day trek in the three named countries. It includes nature walks at Iguazu and Ecuadorian island excursions; high-altitude journeys by 4x4 take place in Bolivia.

### Can we visit both Galapagos island routes?

The current tour includes one of the two marine excursion options. Additional visits must be arranged separately, subject to availability, duration and permits.

### Is the Uruguay section suitable for active-holiday enthusiasts?

It is a varied urban stop, but it does not contain a sporting programme: the published visit is a one-day ferry trip to Montevideo.

### Can I visit Quito without experience of high-altitude trekking?

No independent trek is required during the specified day. However, Quito is at altitude, so wellbeing and walking pace should be considered in advance, particularly where personal medical restrictions apply.

targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_ecuador_uruguay/interests/culture-and-history/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore the cultures of Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  The cultural stages of a journey through Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay connect the cities of the Río de la Plata with colonial architecture in the Andes. Buenos Aires offers sightseeing and a tango show, Montevideo a one-day guided ferry excursion, and Quito its historic centre, El Panecillo and the Middle of the World attractions. These are parts of a larger eight-country journey, with other eventful stages between Uruguay and Ecuador. Discover which traditions can really be compared and where time for exploring them is limited.
---

## Three countries and two distinct cultural traditions

**Argentina and Uruguay share the history of the Río de la Plata, while Ecuador adds Quito's highland world of Andean and colonial traditions.** Our themed selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It also visits Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia.

Selecting these three countries in the filter does not mean travelling only through them on an uninterrupted route. Buenos Aires and a day in Montevideo are followed by Chile, high-altitude Bolivia and Peru; Quito comes much later in the mainland itinerary.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

| City | Cultural focus |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires | Neighbourhoods, history, tango |
| Montevideo | Old Town and the Río de la Plata |
| Quito | Baroque art, squares, the equator |

## Buenos Aires: neighbourhoods and live tango

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the programme includes a three-hour group sightseeing tour led by a Russian-speaking guide. The route mentions Plaza de Mayo, San Telmo, La Boca, Recoleta and other districts. It is an introduction to the city's port history, the architecture of its central squares and its diverse urban communities, although three hours cannot provide an in-depth exploration of every neighbourhood.

In the evening there is **a tango show with dinner**. This is a substantial part of the cultural itinerary, not a passing reference to tango as a national symbol. Uruguay also shares this tradition: UNESCO added Argentine and Uruguayan tango to the Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2009, linking its development to the urban cultures of Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

On this tour, travellers encounter tango on stage in Argentina. **A separate milonga or musical evening in Uruguay is not listed.** Anyone wishing to compare the two capitals' active dance communities would need to modify the programme and allow more time.

## Montevideo: seeing a neighbouring country in one day

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited the day after the Buenos Aires tour: an early transfer to the port, ferry journey, sightseeing with an English-speaking guide, free time and the return crossing. The itinerary mentions the harbour, Independence Square, Old Town and the cathedral. This provides a worthwhile but brief introduction to the capital.

Consider **the difference between the two countries' shared cultural heritage and the actual depth of the excursions**. After the tango show in Buenos Aires, the Montevideo visit allows mainly for a city overview. The two cities have Río de la Plata traditions in common, but there is little opportunity in this schedule to compare their museums, neighbourhoods and musical life in depth.

Ferry logistics directly affect the day's cultural experience. Boarding, immigration control, travel from the terminal, meeting the guide and departing again all reduce time spent in the city's streets. Travellers hoping to spend an evening in Uruguay should discuss an overnight stay rather than try to fit it into the existing one-day visit.

## Ecuador: Quito's colonial art and the Middle of the World

After several other countries, the extended journey reaches [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). According to the itinerary, the sightseeing day, including transfers, lasts around eight hours. The historic centre includes Plaza Grande, the cathedral, the Jesuit church, the Basilica of the National Vow, San Francisco Square and a panorama from El Panecillo.

Quito's historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Its colonial urban fabric is well preserved, and the so-called Quito School blended European and local artistic traditions. This sets the Ecuadorian stage apart from the city history of Buenos Aires and Montevideo. Look beyond façade photographs to the interiors of churches, carved details and religious art.

The same excursion includes **Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum**. The monument and museum explore the history of geographical measurements, understandings of the equator line and regional cultures. Museum demonstrations should be viewed as part of the exhibition; entertaining experiments are not a substitute for precise geodetic measurements.

Quito lies high in the Andes. Even walking through its old streets feels different from an excursion in the Río de la Plata lowlands. The day's plan combines the historic centre, a viewpoint and a trip outside the city, so lunch breaks and the order of stops matter.

## Cultural days outside the selected three countries

To appreciate the full scope of the product, remember its other destinations. The same [eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes Peru with Machu Picchu and Cusco, Bolivia with Tiwanaku, Brazil with Rio, and Colombia with historical and city excursions. These stages cannot be removed from the overall duration while still promising the same range of experiences.

If your main interests are **tango, Quito's colonial art and the neighbouring capitals of the Río de la Plata**, a shorter custom itinerary could be designed. Flights, overnight stays and excursion conditions would have to be calculated separately. For single-country comparisons, browse [Argentina cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/), [Ecuador cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/) and [Uruguay cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/uruguay/).

For a broad introduction to the continent, compare this themed selection with the [general Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador_uruguay/) and [multi-country cultural journeys](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Preserving time for excursions amid complex logistics

The two Río de la Plata capitals share a maritime and river transport geography; Quito involves very different altitude and a long journey from the southern mainland. To remember the experiences rather than only the transfers, calculate travel time from hotel to hotel, allowing for ports, airports, luggage and possible delays.

Documentation for each country and transit stage must be checked against nationality and the final route. A visit to Ecuador and a subsequent journey to the Galapagos have their own practical requirements; addressing those is separate from planning the mainland's cultural sightseeing.

Ada Tours helps coordinate transport, realistic excursion days and sufficient time to get to know the cities. **If culture is the main interest, adding a full day in the right city is preferable to expanding the list of countries without time to explore them.**

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel in these three countries

### Is there tango in both Argentina and Uruguay?

Tango belongs to the cultural heritage of both countries. In the published itinerary, a tango show with dinner is included in Buenos Aires, while Uruguay features a Montevideo sightseeing tour without a separate dance event.

### Can I see Quito on the same day as Montevideo?

No. They are different stages of the eight-country journey. The itinerary travels through Chile, Bolivia and Peru in between; a separate three-country trip would need a new flight plan.

### How much time is allocated to historic Quito?

The excursion day, including transfers, takes around eight hours and covers the Old Town, El Panecillo, Mitad del Mundo and Intiñan. It is a broad overview; an additional day could be discussed for a more relaxed museum visit.

### Will this selection appeal to lovers of colonial architecture?

Yes, particularly thanks to Quito's historic centre. Buenos Aires and Montevideo offer a different focus: neighbourhoods, port history and Río de la Plata culture. The [full tour itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) shows the precise order of visits.

targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_ecuador_uruguay/interests/nature/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "See the nature stops in Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay overlap within an extensive 32-day Ada Tours journey. Nature experiences, however, are unevenly distributed: travellers visit Iguazu in Argentina, spend a sightseeing day in Montevideo in Uruguay, and travel to the Galapagos Islands in Ecuador. Discover where the nature programme actually takes place, why countries cannot be judged by a single thematic tag and how to choose a journey focused on islands.
---

## Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay: different roles for three countries in one trip

**The main nature highlights of this combination are in Argentina and Ecuador.** Argentina offers [Iguazu Falls](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), while Ecuador offers the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Uruguay is primarily represented by a sightseeing trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), where visitors can see the shores of the Río de la Plata but do not have a separate national-park excursion scheduled.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). This is not a standalone tour limited to Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay. Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia are also visited along the way. Together, they form the travel stages between the Río de la Plata and Ecuador.

This route suits travellers who want to combine South America's celebrated waterfalls with Pacific island ecosystems and city visits. For several days on Uruguay's Atlantic coast, however, you would need an itinerary with overnight stays in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/), which are not included here.

## Argentina: waterfalls, not glaciers

During the early stages, travellers see Iguazu from both sides of the border: [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) in Brazil and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina. On both sides, paths pass through humid vegetation, while different viewing points reveal the scale and layout of the waterfall system.

The Argentine-side excursion takes place on day seven. It is followed by a flight to Buenos Aires, where the itinerary shifts to historic neighbourhoods, architecture and tango. **Patagonia, El Calafate and Perito Moreno Glacier are not included in the Argentine section of this tour.** They should not be expected merely because they feature elsewhere on the Ada Tours website.

Weather and trail conditions at the falls can change, so comfortable shoes and clothing suitable for high humidity are important. The forest's biodiversity does not mean guaranteed sightings of jaguars or other rare wildlife. The visit focuses primarily on the cascades themselves.

## Uruguay: Montevideo in one day

On day nine, travellers take the ferry from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), explore Uruguay's capital and return to Argentina. Montevideo's Rambla stretches along the water, and the visit offers views of the broad Río de la Plata and life in the coastal neighbourhoods.

Nevertheless, this stop **does not become a nature expedition**. There is no dedicated marine-wildlife excursion, visit to Uruguay's national parks or multi-day beach stay. Although Montevideo is surrounded by water, the day's principal purpose is sightseeing in the city.

Uruguay serves a different purpose: it adds the experience of another country between the Argentine and Chilean sections. That is valuable on an extensive continental journey, but travellers primarily interested in empty beaches and wildlife watching should consider a more in-depth Uruguay itinerary.

## Ecuador: the principal island-nature programme

Before Ecuador, the route travels through Chile, Bolivia and Peru. After a flight from Lima, travellers explore [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) before continuing to the [Galapagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Day 23 brings arrival on [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and its highland areas, followed by a separate island excursion the next day.

An important detail is that there is **a choice of routes**, not four visits in one day. The options are [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and [Bachas](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/), or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and [Cape Carrion](/ecuador/place/punta-carrion/). The actual itinerary depends on the arrangements and must be agreed beforehand. The next stage returns travellers to the mainland via Guayaquil.

On the Galapagos, visitors must follow designated routes and the instructions of authorised guides. Animals must not be approached at will or fed; the island ecosystem is protected. Which species are seen depends on the excursion, season and animal behaviour. **A realistic aim is to visit the specified island sites, not a guarantee of encountering every species.**

## Comparing the nature experiences

| Country | What the programme includes |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazu on the Argentine side |
| Uruguay | Montevideo, the city and Rambla |
| Ecuador | Santa Cruz and the selected Galapagos excursion |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

This comparison shows why the tour's general nature theme does not apply equally to every country. Argentina and Ecuador have clearly identified natural experiences, while the Uruguay stage is a city excursion. Travellers may value it just as highly, but should understand the purpose of that day.

## An eight-country itinerary and practical preparation

The journey begins in Brazil, continues through Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Montevideo, travels across Chile, Bolivia and Peru, reaches Ecuador and ends in Colombia. It cannot be planned as a simple direct Argentina–Uruguay–Ecuador flight itinerary: the other countries already form part of the product.

For Iguazu, protection against moisture is useful; for the highlands of Bolivia and Peru, allow for acclimatisation, warm clothing and sun protection; for the Galapagos, follow biosecurity rules and protected-area restrictions. Passport and visa requirements must be checked separately for each traveller's nationality and the sequence of border crossings, including re-entry into Argentina after Uruguay.

If the islands matter more than the other countries, start by exploring [Ecuador nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/ecuador/) and comparing the number of actual days on the archipelago. The extended itinerary offers a broad overview, but does not replace a separate long stay in the Galapagos.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a national-park excursion included in Uruguay?

No. The programme confirms a Montevideo sightseeing excursion with a return to Buenos Aires; no separate Uruguayan nature park appears on the itinerary.

### Are both pairs of Galapagos islands guaranteed?

No. The island stage offers alternatives: North Seymour with Bachas, or South Plaza with Cape Carrion. The actual choice is confirmed when organising the trip.

### Can Iguazu and the Galapagos be combined in one tour?

Yes. Both attractions feature in the [32-day programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), but several other countries and many excursions lie between them.

status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore wildlife and nature stages of the itinerary"
lead: >-
  Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay offer different natural settings, but wildlife experiences are unevenly distributed across the current 32-day itinerary. Argentina brings subtropical forest and Iguazu Falls, while Ecuador offers the Galapagos Islands, seabirds and island ecosystems. Uruguay is represented by a sightseeing visit to Montevideo, without a separate wildlife-watching programme. Choosing correctly between the two possible Galapagos marine excursions is particularly important.

## Where to look for wildlife on this itinerary

Our themed Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. This is an [extensive journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) that also visits Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. **Nature is a primary theme of the tour, while animal watching is a secondary one. That does not mean wildlife watching takes place in each of the three selected countries.**

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

For this particular trio, the nature experience centres on two clear highlights: [Iguazu Falls in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Ecuador's Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). A one-day visit to Montevideo lies between them, followed by an extended journey through other South American countries.

| Country | Actual experience |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Waterfalls and subtropical forest |
| Uruguay | City visit to Montevideo |
| Ecuador | Galapagos Islands and boat excursion |

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls and the forest around them

Near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), travellers visit the Argentine side of the falls in a group with a Russian-speaking guide. The programme visits the Brazilian side the previous day. These are two different perspectives on the same natural system, but the excursions take place in separate national parks.

Argentina's Iguazu National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Its waterfalls are surrounded by subtropical forest with diverse plants, birds and mammals. **The excursion offers the experience of the natural landscape along an accessible route, not a guaranteed encounter with a particular animal species.** Sightings depend on weather, timing and animal behaviour.

Do not confuse the Argentine excursion with optional attractions across the border in Brazil. The programme separately mentions the Bird Park and Macuco Safari as additional activities. They cannot automatically be treated as included in the price or as part of the Argentine nature day. When choosing, compare actual time spent in each park and the status of optional experiences.

## Why the Uruguay stage is not a wildlife safari

After Buenos Aires, travellers take a ferry excursion to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) with an English-speaking guide. The itinerary includes city sightseeing, free time and a return to Argentina. **This tour does not advertise Uruguayan nature reserves or whale-, bird- or marine-mammal-watching excursions.**

Uruguay appears in the selection because it is one of the primary countries of the multi-country route, while the route as a whole includes animal watching at other stages. A country on the map and a thematic label for the tour do not create a dedicated wildlife programme there.

A separate nature stage in Uruguay would need to be arranged as an itinerary change, with additional days and a specific destination. Those primarily interested in the confirmed nature experiences rather than city stops should compare [Argentina nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/) and [Ecuador wildlife-watching tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz and a choice of one island itinerary

The Ecuadorian section begins in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) and continues with a flight to the Galapagos. After arriving on Baltra, travellers transfer to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), cross its highlands and stay near Puerto Ayora. The programme includes an excursion through the island's highlands and lava tunnels.

UNESCO recognises the Galapagos as one of the world's most important natural sites because of island evolution, marine ecosystems and endemic species. The archipelago contains varied habitats, so nearby islands offer different chances to see birds, sea lions, iguanas and other wildlife. **The specific landing site matters more than the general word 'Galapagos' in a tour title.**

Under the current programme, the following day includes **one of two alternative boat excursions**. The final choice is confirmed after booking:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and [Bachas Beach](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/). The route description highlights frigatebirds, blue-footed boobies and sea lions on the island, with a lagoon and opportunities to swim and snorkel at Bachas. More details appear on the [North Seymour excursion page](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/).
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrion. This option features a walk among island vegetation, opportunities to observe sea lions and land iguanas, followed by time on the water near the cape. The conditions are described on the [South Plaza excursion page](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/).

These are **alternatives for a single excursion day**. Listing North Seymour, Bachas, South Plaza and Cape Carrion in the catalogue does not mean all four locations will be visited. Nor does mentioning particular animals in an island description promise an encounter with each of them.

## Watching wildlife responsibly

The Galapagos operate under a special conservation regime. Access to locations, vessel routes and landing rules are subject to authorisation. Travellers therefore need to confirm their island excursion in advance, follow guides' instructions, stay on designated routes and avoid interfering with wildlife. An attractive photograph in a description cannot guarantee that a bird or sea lion will be in the same place on the day of your visit.

When choosing between the two options, consider not only the desired animals but also the length of the boat journey, landing conditions, walking difficulty, possible snorkelling and your tolerance for rough seas. Binoculars and a camera with a suitable lens are preferable for photographing birds to attempting to approach an animal.

Altitude, humidity, sun exposure and transport conditions also change between Quito and the islands. The clothes suitable for exploring Quito's historic centre are different from those needed aboard a boat in the Pacific.

## Choosing a nature itinerary without false expectations

**If your priorities are waterfalls and island wildlife, Argentina and Ecuador are the most important countries in this programme.** The Montevideo city day adds cultural variety but reduces the time available for nature watching. The eight-country format adds Bolivia's highland lagoons and other landscapes, but requires frequent journeys between countries.

Before booking, decide whether dramatic landscapes, birdwatching, marine wildlife or a slower pace with several nature outings matters most. We help match these priorities to the published itinerary, choose a sequence of flights and agree on an available island excursion option. A customised journey can also be discussed, but its contents, duration and price will differ.

Other options for comparison appear in our [multi-country wildlife trips](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) and the [general Argentina, Ecuador and Uruguay selection](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador_uruguay/). These help distinguish countries included by geography from activities confirmed in an actual itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about nature and wildlife in these three countries

### Can we see wildlife in all three countries?

The programme includes island wildlife watching in the Galapagos, while the Argentine visit to Iguazu is focused on waterfalls and forest scenery. Uruguay includes a Montevideo city tour without a separate nature-reserve excursion.

### Do travellers visit both North Seymour and South Plaza?

No. The programme offers one of two island alternatives. The option is confirmed after booking; adding other islands would require a separate itinerary change.

### Are blue-footed booby sightings guaranteed?

No. The bird is characteristic of the archipelago and mentioned in the excursion description, but encounters with wild animals depend on natural conditions.

### Is there time in the Galapagos besides the boat excursion?

Yes. The day before the marine excursion includes arrival on Santa Cruz and exploration of its highlands, followed later by the return flight via Guayaquil. The complete sequence is described in the [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

## Argentina and Peru: combining Buenos Aires with Machu Picchu

**Argentina and Peru make it possible to discover modern South American cities, glaciers and ancient Andean monuments on one journey.** In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), visitors can explore neighbourhoods and tango culture. In southern Argentina, near [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), lies a world of glaciers and lakes. In Peru, the itinerary takes travellers through [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

**Argentina and Peru have no common land border.** An overland journey between them goes through Bolivia or Chile, while flying is the principal way to travel on many routes. It is therefore important to review the full country sequence: additional stops between the Argentine and Peruvian stages may include Brazil, Chile and Bolivia.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Peru among the principal countries visited. This also covers programmes with further main destinations. The filter's name **does not mean a tour necessarily visits exactly two countries**.

For a cultural introduction to Argentina and Peru, allow sufficient days for Buenos Aires, Cusco and Machu Picchu. Adding Patagonia makes logistics much more complex: another domestic flight and time for excursions will be needed. Adding Iguazu, Atacama or Uyuni turns the journey into a broader trip across the continent.

## Flights and transport: two possible directions

On the [14-day private itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/), Argentina comes before Peru: after Buenos Aires, travellers head to Lima. The order is reversed on the [15-day group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/): Peru comes first, followed by Argentina and Patagonia. The two journeys differ in their attractions and in the time devoted to transport.

International flights between different parts of the continent must be coordinated with domestic services. Buenos Aires has Ezeiza International Airport (EZE) and the more central Aeroparque (AEP); changing airports may require another transfer and a fresh check-in. For Peru, Lima, Cusco and the journey to Machu Picchu must be planned separately. **Do not assume a direct connection, a single ticket or included baggage until the selected fare confirms it.**

Road transfers, domestic flights and rail journeys each need different time allowances. If a flight arrives in the evening, booking an early paid admission to an archaeological site for the next morning can be risky. Ada Tours helps coordinate the day's sequence and ground transfers around actual schedules.

## Visas and connections: what Russian citizens should check

According to the Argentine Ministry of Foreign Affairs' official treaty register, checked on 15 October 2026, the visa-free travel agreement between Russia and Argentina remains in force. Short visits by holders of ordinary Russian international passports fall under the relevant arrangements, but permitted stay, passport requirements and reasons for entry must comply with the rules in force.

**Peru maintains its own official list of visa exemptions for foreign citizens**, including conditions determined by passport type and purpose of travel. Argentine rules do not automatically extend to Peru. Before purchasing tickets, check current requirements for every participant's nationality: passport validity, proof of onward travel, required documents and the permitted length of stay.

Remember the third countries too. Ada Tours' ready-made itineraries frequently include Brazil; others travel through Chile and Bolivia. Collecting baggage during a connection, checking in again or changing airports may mean passing through immigration control in a transit country. When re-entering a country already visited, the rules applying to that second border crossing also matter.

We help work out the country sequence, prepare a document checklist and allow time for borders and airports. Decisions on visa issuance and permission to enter remain with the relevant authorities.

## Machu Picchu: entry route and timing

**A visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) requires an admission ticket arranged in advance for a particular date, time and circuit.** Peru's Ministry of Culture uses the Tu Boleto system. Since September 2026, the ministry has been introducing a direct sales mechanism with payment confirmation, so purchasing arrangements and availability should be checked when booking.

The archaeological site offers different visitor circuits. A ticket for one circuit does not automatically grant access to the others. Planning must connect admission time with transport from [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the journey to Machu Picchu and the return. A poorly timed connection could cost a full day on an already busy multi-country itinerary.

If the tour also includes [Puno and Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), that is a separate high-altitude stage. It cannot simply be added to a Machu Picchu excursion as a short stop along the way. Check how many nights the itinerary allocates to Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Titicaca.

## Peru's altitude and Argentina's seasons

[Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is approximately 3,350 metres above sea level. Altitude can be felt particularly strongly after low-lying [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) or [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Even physically fit travellers may experience headaches, disturbed sleep or weakness. During the first days at altitude, choose gentler activities and avoid overloading the schedule. Anyone with heart or lung conditions or a history of altitude-related problems should discuss the trip with a doctor beforehand.

Peru and Argentina also have different seasons. For trekking and archaeological visits around Cusco, the drier period, roughly May to September, is often more convenient. If the Argentine section includes [Patagonia](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), its warmer season is mainly December to March. Strong winds and rain are possible during the southern summer; Peru's rainy season can bring wet trails and difficult road conditions. **There is no single ideal month for both parts of the itinerary.**

For a tour focusing on Buenos Aires and Cusco, dates can primarily be chosen around Peru. For a trip including El Calafate, first consider Patagonia's seasonal accessibility and weather, then check conditions for the Andean stage. Discuss in advance which excursions are actually included on the dates you want.

## Currencies, bank cards and a multi-country travel budget

The local currency in Argentina is the **Argentine peso (ARS)**, and in Peru it is the **Peruvian sol (PEN)**. If the journey includes Brazil, travellers will also need the **Brazilian real (BRL)**. Chile and Bolivia add their own currencies. US-dollar payments and exchange availability depend on the city, bank, exchange office and type of service; there is no universal exchange rate or payment method for the entire journey.

Holders of Russian-issued bank cards need to check whether their **particular cards** work internationally rather than relying on the way payments are handled within Russia. For remote excursion stops, plan a cash reserve, and understand rates and fees for every exchange. Customs rules for carrying and declaring cash must be checked separately in each country.

When comparing tours, examine what is covered: domestic flights, Machu Picchu admission, train tickets, excursions, transfers, meals, hotels and baggage. Private and group options must be compared with participant numbers and DBL/SGL accommodation conditions in mind wherever these are part of the offer. The lowest advertised amount without a list of services gives a poor picture of the real trip cost.

## What to pack and how to avoid an exhausting itinerary

For city days in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), normal comfortable clothing is appropriate. In [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), bring warm layers for mornings and evenings, sun protection and comfortable shoes. Adding [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) means preparing for wind and rain. All of this must fit the actual hand-luggage and baggage allowances of each domestic flight.

If your holiday is short, first choose the essential experiences: Buenos Aires with Machu Picchu, Patagonia with Inca history, or an extended journey through several countries. Then compare not just total duration but the number of travel days, overnight stays, altitude and included services. Ada Tours helps select the order of stops and coordinate sensible time buffers between journeys.

## Frequently asked questions about Argentina and Peru tours

### Can I visit only Argentina and Peru?

Yes, such a journey can be arranged with flights between the countries. However, all the current Ada Tours itineraries in this selection also include other countries. A trip limited strictly to the two requires a separately checked and agreed programme.

### Which destination is better to start with?

On the [14-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/), Argentina comes before Peru, while on the [15-day group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/), it follows Peru. The choice depends on travel dates, airports, Patagonia's season and when you prefer to tackle the high-altitude stage.

### Should Machu Picchu tickets be bought in advance?

Yes, it is best to reserve the specific visitor circuit, date and time in advance. Transport and overnight stays are planned around the ticket; buying one does not provide access to every circuit in the archaeological complex.

### Does spending a week in Buenos Aires help with acclimatisation to Cusco's altitude?

No. Spending time in a low-altitude city is not altitude acclimatisation. The ascent to Cusco calls for separate planning of activity levels, rest and medical restrictions.

### Can I use one bank card in all countries?

That depends on the issuing bank, card network and particular country. Argentina and Peru use different currencies, and tours including Brazil add a third. Check that your card works and have a backup payment method.
